reconcile.note: Gill fuses the two reasons by reading 'for your sakes' as Moses' own sin at Meribah, which the people's provocation had itself brought about.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "What angered God so much that he didn't allow Moses to enter the promised land?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/angered-god.html) (2013).

sides.snippet: Yahweh said to Moses and Aaron, Because you didn't believe in me, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore you shall not bring this assembly into the land which I have given them.
sides.verseText: Yahweh said to Moses and Aaron, Because you didn't believe in me, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore you shall not bring this assembly into the land which I have given them.

sides.snippet: But Yahweh was angry with me for your sakes, and didn't listen to me; and Yahweh said to me, Let it suffice you; speak no more to me of this matter.
sides.verseText: But Yahweh was angry with me for your sakes, and didn't listen to me; and Yahweh said to me, Let it suffice you; speak no more to me of this matter.
